statement: In an arithmetic sequence, the $4$th term is $23$ and the $11$th term is $58$. What is the $30$th term?

choices.misconception: I correctly counted 19 steps of 5, but I started from the 4th term, 23, instead of from the 11th term.
I counted 18 steps from the 11th term to the 30th instead of 19, so I got 58 + 18 × 5 = 148.
I found the common difference 5 and then assumed the nth term is just 5n, forgetting the starting value.
I counted 20 steps from the 11th term to the 30th instead of 19, so I got 58 + 20 × 5 = 158.

hints: Going from the $4$th term to the $11$th term takes $7$ equal steps.
From the $11$th term to the $30$th term there are $19$ more steps of $5$.

solutions.reliable: From the $4$th term to the $11$th term there are $11 - 4 = 7$ steps, covering $58 - 23 = 35$, so the common difference is $5$. From the $11$th term to the $30$th term there are $30 - 11 = 19$ steps, so the $30$th term is $58 + 19 \cdot 5 = 153$.
solutions.elegant: The first term is $23 - 3 \cdot 5 = 8$, so the $n$th term is $8 + 5(n - 1) = 5n + 3$. Check: $5 \cdot 4 + 3 = 23$ and $5 \cdot 11 + 3 = 58$. The $30$th term is $5 \cdot 30 + 3 = 153$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
